flawed_step: The claim fails at the attempted inference that pairwise distinct arc capacities force a unique minimum cut. Distinct individual capacities do not distinguish cuts, particularly when isolated vertices may be placed on either side.
counterexample: Let V={s,t,a,b}, with the single arc s→t of capacity 1; a and b are isolated. This is a loopless digraph on exactly four vertices, its sole capacity is a positive integer, and the capacities are pairwise distinct. Its maximum s-t flow is exactly 1. The four distinct cuts {s}, {s,a}, {s,b}, and {s,a,b} each have capacity 1, since s→t is the only crossing arc. Hence all four are minimum cuts.
assessment_summary: The statement is false. The explicit network satisfies every hypothesis but has four distinct minimum s-t cuts.
